content.text:
`./index.html` is written and is the only file in the working directory. Both self-check vectors match. The strategy averages **47.38 waves** on 600 seeds I held out from tuning, against 25.38 for the reference vector-A strategy.

**What I verified** (the checks ran on the scripts copied out of the finished `index.html`):
- **Vector A:** 25.38, fall tick 1035, 166 log entries, hash `82a5353d`. Exact match.
- **Vector B:** 10.93, fall tick 457, 48 entries, hash `2e8858d7`. Exact match.
- **Strategy script:** adds exactly one global (`createStrategy`), returns a fresh object on each call, and uses no forbidden APIs. A full game takes about 8 ms on average (21 ms worst) in JavaScriptCore.
- **Seed 42 (2020 ticks):** score 46.93 with the fall at tick 1897 (94.85 s), so the collapse happens inside the replay. Repeated runs give the same hash, `5cf5106f`.
- **Strategy score:** 47.37 mean on seeds 1000–1299 and 47.39 on seeds 5000–5299 (range 44.0–49.7). None of these seeds, nor seed 42, were used for tuning.

**How the strategy works.** I tuned it with parallel hill-climbing in a copy of the engine, on separate training seeds.
- **Build:** a fixed build order that ends with 10 cannons, 4 flak, 1 lance, 1 bolt and 1 frost, all at tier 3. Early on it holds back gold to earn interest, and spends it straight away when hurt enemies get close to the keep.
- **Targeting:** cannons and flak aim where their splash does the most useful damage, without overkill, and go for menders and runners first. The other turrets weigh effective damage, how close the enemy is to the exit, and whether the shot kills.
- **Cooldown resets:** a new turret's cooldown starts at 0, and selling refunds 70%. So late in the game, at the start of a wave, it sells, rebuilds and re-upgrades a busy cannon whose next shot would otherwise come too late in that wave. To time this exactly, it works out the current tick inside `target()` from how far enemies have moved since the last plan; in testing, none of 448 resets was wasted.
- **Biggest finding:** with unlimited gold the original build order scored the same as with normal gold. So the fully upgraded board was the limit, not the economy, and the gains came from the turret mix, targeting and resets.

**Browser testing.** I only tested in headless Firefox on an Apple M1, not Chrome, and the page ran with zero errors.
- **Playback controls:** a scripted test drove every state change (countdown 3-2-1, pause and play, the 0.1 s frame-time cap, speed buttons, Re-fire's 1 s hold, scrubbing, ending, restarting from the end). All behaved as specified. The same `simTime` reached through different scrub orders produced identical pixels.
- **Visual checks:** screenshots at 1920×1080 and 1280×650 confirmed the board fits with the dock and HUD clear, the unit types are distinguishable at the smaller size, and the fall (collapse, shockwave, fade to grey) renders.
- **`measuredFps` is 114**, but that is how fast the scene renders in a tight loop (busy late-game frames with 200+ enemies, headless Firefox, M1). It is not a real 60/120 Hz measurement in Chrome on a discrete GPU.

**Things to know:**
- **Audio is untested.** I built all the required sounds, but I never heard them; headless testing can't play sound.
- **The fade to grey uses a CSS filter.** The post-fall desaturation is a CSS filter on `#stage` driven by `simTime`, not a WebGL pass.
- **The fall ends the replay at 100 s.** The scene freezes and greys out from 94.85 s; effects still in flight then finish on their own rather than freezing.
- **Reset visuals.** The sell-and-rebuild resets are drawn as a small blue flash at the slot instead of a rubble collapse each time, so the late game doesn't fill up with rubble effects.
- **Extra global.** The main script also exposes `window.__rampart`, a small debugging handle I used for testing.

All of these are also recorded in `window.BENCH_REPORT`.
